skills.name: Establish subtraction-ready form
skills.definition: Prepare quantities for subtraction by rewriting numbers into a compatible form, including matching denominators and normalizing whole or mixed numbers into subtraction-ready representations.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory setup skills that occur before core subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making the operands subtraction-ready. They are sometimes distinct, but at this coarser level the diagnostic distinction between denominator alignment and number-form normalization is less important than separating setup from execution.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole-number parts in mixed-number problems.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because this is the core execution step and has strong independent diagnostic value. Students may be able to prepare numbers correctly yet still make subtraction errors.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole-number part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to continue subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because borrowing/regrouping produces distinctive error patterns and is not required in all mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction items. It remains diagnostically meaningful apart from ordinary subtraction.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms or simplify it to a whole number or zero when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a post-subtraction transformation with its own common error patterns, such as failing to reduce or mishandling zero.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: Assemble the final stated result by combining whole-number and fractional parts or omitting zero parts when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final composition is a distinct answer-formatting step, especially in mixed-number items where students may compute parts correctly but fail to present the final form.

skills.name: Establish subtraction-ready form
skills.definition: Prepare quantities for subtraction by rewriting numbers into a compatible form, including matching denominators and normalizing whole or mixed numbers into subtraction-ready representations.
skills.merge_rationale: Inherited from the K=5 level. These skills belong to the same preparation phase and are naturally merged at coarser granularity.

skills.name: Execute subtraction and regroup if needed
skills.definition: Perform subtraction on aligned whole and fractional parts, including regrouping or borrowing across whole and fractional parts when the fractional part of the minuend is too small.
skills.merge_rationale: S04 is a conditional extension of S03 during execution: borrowing only arises when direct subtraction of aligned parts is insufficient. In practice, these two skills are tightly coupled within the same execution phase, and S04 depends on the subtraction state created by S03. At this coarser level, combining ordinary subtraction and regrouped subtraction preserves a meaningful distinction between execution and post-processing.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or simplify it to a whole number or zero when appropriate.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification remains a distinct post-processing operation with diagnostic value independent of subtraction execution.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: State the final result in appropriate form by combining whole and fractional parts or omitting unnecessary zero parts.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final answer composition is still distinguishable from simplification: a student may simplify correctly yet fail to express the answer in proper mixed-number, whole-number, or fraction form.

aggregation_notes: The main aggregation principle was to preserve broad problem-solving phases: preparation, execution, post-processing, and final expression. For K=5, the two setup skills (matching denominators and normalizing number form) were merged because both serve to make operands subtraction-ready and are often adjacent preparatory actions. Borrowing was kept separate from ordinary subtraction because it has distinctive error patterns and is not universally required. For K=4, borrowing was merged with subtraction because it is a conditional execution move that arises within the subtraction phase once aligned subtraction reveals insufficiency in the fractional part. Simplification and final answer composition were not merged, since the dossiers show they can occur separately and support different feedback: reduction to lowest terms versus expressing the result in the correct final form.
